analysis.evidence: פְּרִי is in construct with הָעֵץ, yielding “the fruit of the tree.” The prohibition לֹא תֹאכְלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ (“you shall not eat from it”) confirms the literal sense.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וּ־ + preposition מִן (realized as מִ־ with nun assimilated to פ) + masculine singular construct noun פְּרִי.

analysis.evidence: In וּמִפְּרִי הָעֵץ, “and from the fruit of the tree,” הָעֵץ names the tree that bears the fruit. The clause אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן identifies it by its location in the middle of the garden.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + masculine singular absolute noun.

analysis.evidence: אֲשֶׁר introduces the verbless relative clause אֲשֶׁר בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן, “which is in the middle of the garden,” identifying הָעֵץ, “the tree,” by its location.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected relative particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: בְּתוֹךְ הַגָּן means “in the midst of the garden.” The phrase locates הָעֵץ, the tree whose fruit is under discussion.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הַ־ + common noun, common gender, singular absolute.

analysis.evidence: אֱלֹהִים is the subject of אָמַר. The woman quotes God’s words beginning with לֹא תֹאכְלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ, “you shall not eat from it.”
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In אָמַר אֱלֹהִים (“God said”), the third-person masculine singular verb אָמַר presents God as the single speaker. The woman attributes the prohibition against eating or touching the fruit to him.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural common noun in the absolute state, with singular reference.

analysis.evidence: אָמַר אֱלֹהִים (“God said”) introduces the command. לֹא negates the second-person masculine plural imperfect תֹאכְלוּ in לֹא תֹאכְלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ (“you shall not eat from it”).
analysis.morphology: Hebrew negative particle with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: לֹא negates תֹאכְלוּ, giving the prohibition ‘you shall not eat.’ The phrase וּמִפְּרִי הָעֵץ identifies the tree’s fruit as what they are forbidden to eat.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, second person masculine plural

analysis.evidence: וְלֹא תִגְּעוּ בּוֹ means “and you shall not touch it.” The complement בּוֹ refers to the tree and identifies what the addressees are forbidden to touch.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, second person masculine plural, used with לֹא to express a prohibition.

analysis.evidence: After the prohibitions against eating and touching, פֶּן introduces תְּמֻתוּן, “you may die.” Death is the outcome the prohibitions aim to prevent.
פֶּן תְּמֻתוּן means “lest you die.” The verb addresses the same group as תֹאכְלוּ (“you eat”) and תִגְּעוּ (“you touch”). Death is the consequence the warning seeks to avert.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, second person masculine plural, with paragogic nun (־וּן).
analysis.sense: die, come to the end of life
